questions.q: A projectile is fired with a velocity of $20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Find its horizontal range. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explain:
The formula for the horizontal range is $R = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$.
Substitute $u = 20\text{ m/s}$ and $\theta = 30^\circ$:
$R = \frac{20^2 \sin(2 \times 30^\circ)}{10} = \frac{400 \sin 60^\circ}{10} = 40 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ m}$.

questions.q: A stone is projected with a velocity of $20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Calculate the total time of flight. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explain:
The time of flight is given by $T = \frac{2u \sin \theta}{g}$.
Substitute the given values: $T = \frac{2 \times 20 \sin 30^\circ}{10} = 4 \times 0.5 = 2.0\text{ s}$.

questions.q: A ball is thrown horizontally at $15\text{ m/s}$ from the top of a tower $20\text{ m}$ high. Find the horizontal distance from the base of the tower to where it hits the ground. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explain:
First, calculate the time to fall using $h = \frac{1}{2}gt^2$.
$20 = \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 \implies 20 = 5t^2 \implies t^2 = 4 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$.
The horizontal distance (range) is horizontal velocity $\times$ time: $x = u \times t = 15 \times 2 = 30\text{ m}$.

questions.q: A projectile has a maximum height exactly equal to its horizontal range. Find its angle of projection.
questions.explain:
Maximum height $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$ and Range $R = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g} = \frac{2u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g}$.
Given $H = R$, we have $\frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g} = \frac{2u^2 \sin\theta \cos\theta}{g}$.
Canceling $\frac{u^2}{g}$ (and one $\sin\theta$, assuming $\theta > 0$) gives: $\frac{\sin\theta}{2} = 2\cos\theta \implies \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = 4 \implies \tan\theta = 4$.
The angle is $\tan^{-1}(4)$.

questions.q: The path of a projectile is given by the equation $y = x - \frac{x^2}{40}$, where $x$ and $y$ are horizontal and vertical distances in meters respectively. Calculate the horizontal range of the projectile.
questions.explain:
The horizontal range is the horizontal distance travelled when the projectile returns to its initial vertical level ($y = 0$).
Set $y = 0$: $x - \frac{x^2}{40} = 0 \implies x\left(1 - \frac{x}{40}\right) = 0$.
Since $x = 0$ is the starting point, the range is when $1 - \frac{x}{40} = 0 \implies x = 40\text{ m}$.

questions.q: A projectile is fired with an initial speed of $40\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Calculate its maximum height. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explain:
The maximum height is given by $H = \frac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g}$.
Substitute the values: $H = \frac{40^2 (\sin 30^\circ)^2}{2(10)} = \frac{1600 (0.5)^2}{20} = \frac{1600 (0.25)}{20} = \frac{400}{20} = 20\text{ m}$.

questions.q: At what angle of projection does a projectile achieve its maximum horizontal range for a given initial speed?
questions.explain: The horizontal range is $R = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$. The range is maximum when $\sin 2\theta = 1$, which means $2\theta = 90^\circ$, so $\theta = 45^\circ$.

questions.q: A particle is projected with a velocity of $50\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $60^\circ$ to the horizontal. How long does it take to reach its maximum height? (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explain:
The time to reach maximum height is $t = \frac{u \sin \theta}{g}$.
Substitute the values: $t = \frac{50 \sin 60^\circ}{10} = 5 \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 2.5\sqrt{3}\text{ s}$.

questions.q: A body is projected with an initial velocity of $20\text{ m/s}$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the horizontal. Find its speed at the highest point of its trajectory.
questions.explain:
At the highest point, the vertical component of velocity is zero. The body's speed is purely its horizontal component of velocity, which remains constant.
$v_x = u \cos \theta = 20 \cos 45^\circ = 20\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$.

questions.q: A projectile fired from the origin follows the trajectory path modeled by the equation $y = x\sqrt{3} - 5x^2$, where $x$ and $y$ are horizontal and vertical distances in meters. What is its angle of projection to the horizontal?
questions.explain:
The standard Cartesian equation of a trajectory is $y = x \tan \theta - \frac{gx^2}{2u^2 \cos^2 \theta}$.
By comparing the coefficient of $x$ in the equation with the standard form, $\tan \theta = \sqrt{3}$.
Therefore, $\theta = \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) = 60^\circ$.
